**Talking Points for the Texas Tech K-12 Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program**

**Overview**
- The Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program is designed for students who need a flexible, accredited online K-12 education.
- Available to students outside Texas and Texas residents who want more flexibility than the tuition-free program.
- Students can start at any time—open enrollment, not tied to a traditional school calendar.

**Key Features**
- **Accredited Curriculum:** Texas Tech K-12 is accredited by Cognia and approved by the Texas Education Agency (TEA).
- **Wide Range of Courses:** Includes core subjects, electives, foreign languages, and Advanced Placement (AP) courses.
- **Self-Paced Learning:** Students can work at their own pace, with up to six months to complete each course.
- **Supportive Environment:** Access to Texas-certified teachers, academic advisors, counselors, and technical support.
- **Global Access:** Open to students across the U.S. and internationally.

**Program Benefits**
- **Flexibility:** Learn from anywhere, anytime—ideal for students with unique schedules or frequent travel.
- **Comprehensive Curriculum:** Full access to K-12 courses, including credit recovery and accelerated learning options.
- **Personalized Support:** Teachers and advisors provide guidance and feedback throughout the academic year.
- **Preparation for College and Career:** Develops skills and knowledge for post-secondary success.

**Tuition and Fees (Effective September 1, 2022)**
- **Online Courses:** $300 per course (U.S.), $450 per course (International)
- **Online Credit By Exams:** $80 per exam (U.S. only)
- **Admission Fee:** $200 (U.S.), $250 (International)
- **Miscellaneous Fees:** Print surcharge ($25), transcript request ($5), diploma replacement ($25), overnight shipping ($30, U.S. only)
- **Textbooks:** Most courses include materials, but some (e.g., AP courses) may require separate textbook purchases.

**Enrollment Process**
1. **Apply Online:** Complete the application and provide required documents (birth certificate, transcripts).
   - [Application Link](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/enroll/)
2. **Enrollment Confirmation:** Receive confirmation and meet with an academic advisor for course selection.
3. **Begin Learning:** Start courses at any time and access all online resources.

**Who Should Apply?**
- Non-Texas residents seeking a fully accredited K-12 program.
- Students needing a flexible, non-traditional school setting.
- Homeschool families wanting a structured, online curriculum.

**Technology Requirements**
- Modern computer (≤5 years old), webcam, microphone, broadband internet.
- Supported operating systems: Windows 10+, macOS 11+, ChromeOS, Linux (Ubuntu 18.04+).
- Supported browsers: Latest Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari (macOS only).
- Mobile devices are not recommended as primary devices.

**Additional Information**
- No payment plans; full payment is due upon enrollment.
- Once a student submits an assignment for grading, they are no longer eligible for a refund.
- [More details on Tuition & Fees](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/about/fees/)

**Contact for Questions**
- Phone: 1-800-692-6877
- Email: ttuk12@ttu.edu

**Next Step**
- Visit the [application page](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/enroll/) to get started or contact Texas Tech K-12 for more information.

**Discussion-Based Assessments (DBAs) in Texas Tech K-12**

**What Are Discussion-Based Assessments?**
- Discussion-Based Assessments (DBAs) are live, interactive assessments conducted between the student and teacher.
- They are used to verify student understanding, ensure academic integrity, and provide an opportunity for students to explain their learning in their own words.
- DBAs may be required at certain points in a course, as specified in the course syllabus.

**Purpose of DBAs**
- Confirm that the student, not someone else, is completing the coursework.
- Allow teachers to assess deeper understanding and critical thinking.
- Provide students with feedback and support in a one-on-one setting.
- Address any questions or concerns the student may have about the course material.

**How DBAs Work**
- The teacher will schedule a live session (often via video conference or phone) with the student.
- During the session, the teacher will ask questions related to recent course content, assignments, or concepts.
- Students are expected to respond in their own words and demonstrate their understanding.
- The session may be recorded for quality and verification purposes.

**Expectations for Students**
- Be prepared to discuss recent lessons, assignments, and key concepts.
- Have access to your course materials and notes for reference.
- Participate honestly and independently—do not use unauthorized assistance.
- Dress appropriately if the session is via video (see student attire guidelines).

**Why Are DBAs Important?**
- They help maintain academic integrity in an online environment.
- They ensure students are mastering the material and are ready to move forward.
- Teachers may require a DBA if there are concerns about the authenticity of submitted work.

**What Happens After a DBA?**
- The teacher will provide feedback and may allow the student to proceed with the next part of the course.
- If the teacher determines the student does not have sufficient understanding, additional review or assignments may be required.

**Additional Notes**
- DBAs are a standard part of Texas Tech K-12’s approach to online learning and academic integrity.
- Students should check their course syllabus for specific DBA requirements and scheduling instructions.

If you have questions about DBAs or need to schedule one, contact your course teacher directly through the course communication tools or the Texas Tech K-12 support team at 1-800-692-6877 or ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Texas Tech K-12 Grading System and GPA Tracking**

**Grading System**
- Texas Tech K-12 uses a numerical grading system for courses.
- Grades are converted to letter grades and grade points for GPA calculation as follows:

  | Numerical Grade | Letter Grade | Regular Courses | Honors/AP/Dual Credit Courses |
  |-----------------|-------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
  | 90–100          | A           | 4.0             | 5.0                          |
  | 80–89           | B           | 3.0             | 4.0                          |
  | 75–79           | C           | 2.0             | 3.0                          |
  | 70–74           | D           | 1.0             | 2.0                          |
  | 0–69            | F           | 0.0             | 0.0                          |

**GPA Tracking**
- Texas Tech K-12 calculates a student’s final GPA using eligible coursework that applies toward high school graduation.
- All accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses that apply toward graduation are included in the GPA calculation, except approved physical education substitution credits and local-credit courses.
- Grades transferred from accredited schools are also included in the final GPA unless the course is designated as local credit or graded on a pass/fail basis.
- Weighted GPA is awarded for Honors, Advanced Placement (AP), International Baccalaureate (IB), and Dual Credit/Concurrent Credit courses.

**Class Rank**
- Beginning with 9th grade students enrolling after August 1, 2021, class rank is only calculated and reported for students in the Top 10% of a given class, as required by state law.

**Additional Information**
- Only final course grades are officially reported and recorded.
- For more details on grading and GPA, see the [Texas Tech K-12 Policies](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/policies.php).

- For further assistance, you may contact Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.
